title: Isandro and the Compass
premise: Bram Galloway, a salvage diver who has spent two decades measuring life in miles rather than years, is hired to work a wreck the navy won't discuss—only to find the site abandoned by a vanished government survey team and watched over by Isandro Reyes, a teenage stowaway carrying a brass compass that points not north but toward whatever its holder most fears losing. When the navy returns to erase all witnesses, Bram and Isandro flee into the coastal range with the compass as their only guide, gathering a ragtag found family of outcasts along the way. As the snows close in and the truth of the wreck—a sunken transport full of people the state declared expendable—comes to light, Bram must choose between staying invisible and becoming someone worth following. The story ends at a mountain pass where Bram trades his own escape to get Isandro's testimony out, surviving not by running but by finally standing still and being seen.
about_author: Ulyana Okonkwo is a former maritime archaeologist who spent six seasons diving cold-water wrecks before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure stories about people who survive by disappearing—and what it costs them to come back.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A routine salvage dive on an unmarked wreck off the coast establishes Bram's solitary, transactional life and his rule: never ask who owns what you pull up. He surfaces to find a navy tender watching him from beyond the buoy line. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for freedom.

chapters.title: The Survey Team That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Hired quietly through a fixer to recover equipment left by a government survey team that 'walked off the job,' Bram finds their camp intact—boots by the fire, coffee still in the pot, no tracks leading out. Emotional beat: first crack in his indifference; fear he can't price.

chapters.title: A Boy in the Hold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Searching the wreck itself, Bram discovers Isandro, half-frozen, hiding among the crates—the survey team's unofficial guide, who fled when they began 'taking readings that made the instruments scream.' Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other's survival posture.

chapters.title: The Compass That Lies
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro reveals the brass compass he took from the wreck: it doesn't point north, but toward what its holder most fears losing. For Isandro it points back at the wreck. Bram refuses to touch it. Emotional beat: wonder colliding with denial.

chapters.title: Tender in the Fog
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The navy tender arrives at dawn—not to investigate but to sanitize. Men in civilian gear burn the camp and list Bram's boat for seizure. Bram realizes the vanished team wasn't lost; they were collected. Emotional beat: invisibility revoked, terror without drama.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Carried
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Diving one last time before fleeing, they find the hold's true cargo: sealed manifests naming passengers officially listed as drowned decades ago—people the state wrote off. Emotional beat: grief as evidence; the dead demand accounting.

chapters.title: Upcountry
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They abandon the boat and start inland toward the range, aiming for a pass before snowfall. Bram teaches Isandro his rules of movement; Isandro keeps breaking them by being kind. Emotional beat: reluctant mentorship beginning.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Daughter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At a river crossing they meet Odile, a ferry operator whose father was on the manifest. She joins them when she sees the names. Emotional beat: found family's first member; shared loss becomes shared purpose.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Kettle Bridge
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A roadblock forces them off the highway. Bram talks them past a bored corporal using twenty years of practiced anonymity—but the compass trembles in Isandro's pocket, pointing at Odile. Emotional beat: the cost of lying well.

chapters.title: Readings
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In an old fire lookout, Isandro experiments with the compass and realizes it reacts to the wreck's manifests like a needle to ore—it wants the names delivered somewhere. Bram forbids further experiments. Emotional beat: curiosity versus control; trust strained.

chapters.title: The Man Who Measures Miles
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Flashback chapter: how Bram lost his name, his record, and his reason for counting miles instead of years—a botched contract dive he was paid to forget. Emotional beat: the wall around Bram shown being built, stone by stone.

chapters.title: Hunters Above Treeline
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Pursuers—private contractors, not military—catch them on a scree slope. Odile's quick thinking saves them, but Isandro takes a fall protecting the compass. Emotional beat: the boy stops being baggage and becomes a person they'd bleed for.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Cold Ledge
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sheltering with a disgraced naval archivist living off-grid, they learn the wreck was no accident and the survey team was sent to confirm the manifests were destroyed—they weren't. Emotional beat: the conspiracy gains a face and a paper trail.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. First storm hits early. They shelter in a mine adit where Isandro, feverish, confesses he stowed away on the survey team to find his father's name on the wreck. Emotional beat: vulnerability as strength; the compass now points steadily at Bram.

chapters.title: What Bram Fears Losing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram finally holds the compass. It doesn't point at his boat, his freedom, or his secrets—it points at Isandro. Emotional beat: the loner discovers he has something left to lose, and it terrifies him more than the navy.

chapters.title: The Pass Decision
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With contractors closing from below and weather sealing the high route, they split options: run east to disappear forever, or cross south to the regional archive where the manifests can be entered into public record. Emotional beat: the theme made explicit—invisibility or witness.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They attempt the southern crossing in deteriorating conditions. Rope work, whiteout, Odile nearly lost in a cornice collapse. Emotional beat: found family tested physically; each saves another in turn.

chapters.title: The Archive at Alder Creek
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They reach the archive town, but the clerk is already compromised—the navy arrived hours ahead. A standoff in the reading room where Bram offers himself as the sole 'salvage thief' if the manifests are filed. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely for the first time.

chapters.title: Compass True
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Climax. The contractors move; Odile triggers the town's flood siren to bring witnesses; Isandro walks the manifests through the crowd to the filing desk while Bram holds the door. The compass spins wildly, then settles—pointing nowhere, needing nothing. Emotional beat: courage as public act.

chapters.title: After the Snows
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The filing cannot be undone; an inquiry begins. The navy withdraws rather than escalate. Isandro finds his father's name read aloud in open session. Emotional beat: grief given a public container; mourning as victory.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Facing charges reduced to a fine, Bram chooses to stay in Alder Creek instead of vanishing again—repairing boats, teaching Isandro the water. Emotional beat: stillness chosen, not imposed; identity rebuilt from connection.

chapters.title: North by Nothing
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Spring. Bram, Isandro, and Odile dive the wreck openly under inquiry protection, recovering the remains the state abandoned. The compass, inert now, stays aboard as ballast. Final line lands on Bram measuring the year in seasons, not miles. Emotional beat: homecoming without geography.
